claim: From July 2021, eLife will only review manuscripts already published as preprints.
source: From July 2021 eLife will only review manuscripts already published as preprints, and will focus its editorial process on producing public reviews to be posted alongside the preprints.
evidence: This is a direct statement of eLife's policy change with a specific implementation date.

claim: eLife will focus its editorial process on producing public reviews to be posted alongside preprints.
source: From July 2021 eLife will only review manuscripts already published as preprints, and will focus its editorial process on producing public reviews to be posted alongside the preprints.
evidence: This is a direct statement of eLife's new editorial focus.

claim: If a paper eLife is planning to send out to peer review is not already on a preprint server, eLife will post it to bioRxiv or medRxiv on behalf of the authors.
source: If any paper we are planning to send out to peer review is not already on a preprint server, we will post it to bioRxiv or medRxiv (as appropriate) on behalf of the authors.
evidence: This is a direct statement of eLife's policy for handling manuscripts not yet posted as preprints.

claim: Many authors who previously did not post preprints did so out of inertia rather than opposition.
source: We expect that many of our authors who previously did not post preprints did so out of inertia rather than opposition, and will now do so.
evidence: This is eLife's expectation about author behavior, representing their interpretation of past author motivations.

claim: Some potential authors have real concerns about posting preprints.
source: However, we are aware that some potential authors have real concerns about posting preprints, and others are restricted from doing so for various reasons.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of known concerns among authors.

claim: Some authors are restricted from posting preprints for various reasons.
source: However, we are aware that some potential authors have real concerns about posting preprints, and others are restricted from doing so for various reasons.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of known restrictions on authors.

claim: Adoption of preprints has lagged behind in some areas.
source: We would like to take some time to understand and, where possible, mitigate these concerns, especially in areas where adoption of preprints has lagged behind.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of preprint adoption in certain research areas.

claim: For the next six months, eLife will give authors of papers under review the option to opt out of posting a preprint.
source: Therefore, for the next six months, we will give authors of papers under review the option to opt out of posting a preprint, and will instead ask them to explain their reasons.
evidence: This is a direct statement of eLife's transitional policy with a specific timeframe.

claim: eLife will ask authors who opt out of posting a preprint to explain their reasons.
source: Therefore, for the next six months, we will give authors of papers under review the option to opt out of posting a preprint, and will instead ask them to explain their reasons.
evidence: This is a direct statement of eLife's data collection approach during the transition period.

claim: After the six-month period, eLife will move to only review papers that are already available as preprints.
source: Once we feel we understand and have addressed concerns about preprinting that are in our power to address, we will move to only review papers that are already available as preprints.
evidence: This is a statement of eLife's planned future policy after the transition period.

claim: It will be possible for authors to request a waiver of the preprint-only policy in exceptional circumstances.
source: It will still be possible for authors to request a waiver of this policy in exceptional circumstances, but we expect these to be rare.
evidence: This is a direct statement of eLife's policy exception mechanism.

claim: Waivers of the preprint-only policy are expected to be rare.
source: It will still be possible for authors to request a waiver of this policy in exceptional circumstances, but we expect these to be rare.
evidence: This is eLife's expectation about the frequency of policy waivers.

claim: Peer reviews are typically not written for a public audience.
source: One of the biggest challenges we face in implementing this new system is that peer reviews are typically not written for a public audience.
evidence: This is a statement about the current standard practice in peer review.

claim: eLife learned from Preprint Review that informing reviewers that their reviews would be posted on bioRxiv only rarely led them to write their reviews in a different way.
source: We learned from Preprint Review (https://twitter.com/PreprintReview), our current opt-in system for reviewing preprints, that informing reviewers that their reviews would be posted on bioRxiv only rarely led them to write their reviews in a different way.
evidence: This is a finding from eLife's own experience with their Preprint Review system.

claim: Preprint Review is eLife's current opt-in system for reviewing preprints.
source: We learned from Preprint Review (https://twitter.com/PreprintReview), our current opt-in system for reviewing preprints, that informing reviewers that their reviews would be posted on bioRxiv only rarely led them to write their reviews in a different way.
evidence: This is a description of eLife's existing system.

claim: It is very difficult to inspire new editorial and reviewer practices when they are only employed for a small percentage of articles.
source: We also learned that it is very difficult to inspire new editorial and reviewer practices when they are only employed for a small percentage of articles.
evidence: This is a lesson learned from eLife's experience with their opt-in system.

claim: eLife has concluded that they have to go all in for the new system to succeed.
source: We have therefore concluded that we have to go all in for this system to succeed.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn by eLife based on their experiences.

claim: Starting immediately, eLife is instructing its editors and reviewers to prepare public reviews for all manuscripts under consideration.
source: Hence, starting immediately, we are instructing our editors and reviewers to prepare public reviews for all manuscripts under consideration.
evidence: This is a direct statement of eLife's current policy implementation.

claim: eLife has created a new review template.
source: We have created a new review template, updated our instructions for reviewers to capture what we think should and should not be included in public reviews, and have modified our editorial processes to focus on their production.
evidence: This is a statement of an action taken by eLife.

claim: eLife has updated its instructions for reviewers to capture what should and should not be included in public reviews.
source: We have created a new review template, updated our instructions for reviewers to capture what we think should and should not be included in public reviews, and have modified our editorial processes to focus on their production.
evidence: This is a statement of an action taken by eLife.

claim: eLife has modified its editorial processes to focus on the production of public reviews.
source: We have created a new review template, updated our instructions for reviewers to capture what we think should and should not be included in public reviews, and have modified our editorial processes to focus on their production.
evidence: This is a statement of an action taken by eLife.

claim: eLife will be working closely with editors, reviewers, authors and readers to improve both the process by which public reviews are created and their utility.
source: In the coming months, we will be working closely with our editors, reviewers, authors and readers to improve both the process by which public reviews are created, and their utility to the diverse audiences we hope to reach.
evidence: This is a statement of eLife's planned future activities.

claim: eLife will prepare public-facing reviews for every paper under review.
source: While we will prepare public-facing reviews for every paper under review at eLife, authors will retain a degree of control over when these are posted.
evidence: This is a direct statement of eLife's policy.

claim: Authors will retain a degree of control over when public reviews are posted.
source: While we will prepare public-facing reviews for every paper under review at eLife, authors will retain a degree of control over when these are posted.
evidence: This is a direct statement of eLife's policy regarding author control.

claim: For papers that receive a favorable decision from eLife and where authors elect to proceed with eLife, the public review will be posted to the appropriate preprint server within three weeks.
source: For papers that receive a favorable decision from the journal, and where the authors elect to proceed with eLife, the public review will be posted to the appropriate preprint server within three weeks (to allow authors time to prepare a response).
evidence: This is a direct statement of eLife's policy with a specific timeframe.

claim: The three-week delay before posting public reviews is to allow authors time to prepare a response.
source: For papers that receive a favorable decision from the journal, and where the authors elect to proceed with eLife, the public review will be posted to the appropriate preprint server within three weeks (to allow authors time to prepare a response).
evidence: This is an explanation of the rationale for the three-week timeframe.

claim: If eLife editors decide a paper is not appropriate for eLife, authors will be allowed to postpone the posting of the public review until the paper is published elsewhere.
source: However, if our editors decide a paper is not appropriate for eLife, we will, for now, allow authors to postpone the posting of the public review until the paper is published elsewhere.
evidence: This is a direct statement of eLife's current policy for papers not accepted.

claim: Allowing delays in posting negative public reviews will address author fears that negative public reviews will prejudice their ability to publish their work in a journal.
source: Allowing such delays will address a potential major obstacle to adoption – author fears that negative public reviews will prejudice their ability to publish their work in a journal – while ensuring that authors cannot permanently avoid dealing with issues that may have arisen during our review.
evidence: This is eLife's reasoning about how their policy will address a specific concern.

claim: Author fears that negative public reviews will prejudice their ability to publish their work in a journal is a potential major obstacle to adoption of public reviews.
source: Allowing such delays will address a potential major obstacle to adoption – author fears that negative public reviews will prejudice their ability to publish their work in a journal – while ensuring that authors cannot permanently avoid dealing with issues that may have arisen during our review.
evidence: This is eLife's identification of a barrier to adoption of their new system.

claim: The policy of allowing delays ensures that authors cannot permanently avoid dealing with issues that may have arisen during eLife's review.
source: Allowing such delays will address a potential major obstacle to adoption – author fears that negative public reviews will prejudice their ability to publish their work in a journal – while ensuring that authors cannot permanently avoid dealing with issues that may have arisen during our review.
evidence: This is eLife's explanation of how their policy balances different concerns.

claim: eLife expects to move towards the rapid posting of all reviews, irrespective of the associated publishing decision, as they get better at producing constructive public reviews and as authors get more comfortable with the system.
source: However, as we get better at producing constructive public reviews, and as authors get more comfortable with both the idea and our implementation of it, we expect to move towards the rapid posting of all reviews, irrespective of the associated publishing decision.
evidence: This is a statement of eLife's expected future policy evolution.

claim: eLife's long-term goal is to move away from the use of journal titles as the primary measure of the quality of research in science and medicine.
source: As mentioned above, our long-term goal is to move away from the use of journal titles as the primary measure of the quality of research in science and medicine.
evidence: This is a direct statement of eLife's long-term objective.

claim: Journal titles remain important for many researchers as they pursue their careers.
source: However, we know that journal titles remain important for many researchers as they pursue their careers.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of the current state of academic career advancement.

claim: For the foreseeable future, eLife will continue to select a subset of the papers they review for publication in eLife.
source: Thus, while we are developing alternatives, for the foreseeable future, we will continue to select a subset of the papers we review for "publication" in eLife.
evidence: This is a direct statement of eLife's continued practice during the transition period.

claim: After reviews are submitted, eLife editors and reviewers will consult with each other to decide what they wish to convey in the public review.
source: After the reviews on the paper have been submitted, the editors and reviewers will consult with each other to decide: (i) what they wish to convey in the public review; (ii) if the paper is appropriate for publication in eLife.
evidence: This is a description of eLife's editorial process.

claim: After reviews are submitted, eLife editors and reviewers will consult with each other to decide if the paper is appropriate for publication in eLife.
source: After the reviews on the paper have been submitted, the editors and reviewers will consult with each other to decide: (i) what they wish to convey in the public review; (ii) if the paper is appropriate for publication in eLife.
evidence: This is a description of eLife's editorial process.

claim: Authors will be sent a copy of the public review as well as a letter outlining the reasons for the decision regarding publication in eLife.
source: The authors will then be sent a copy of the public review as well as a letter outlining the reasons for the decision regarding publication in eLife: if a revision is invited, this decision letter will list the issues that need to be addressed before the manuscript can be accepted.
evidence: This is a description of eLife's communication process with authors.

claim: If a revision is invited, the decision letter will list the issues that need to be addressed before the manuscript can be accepted.
source: The authors will then be sent a copy of the public review as well as a letter outlining the reasons for the decision regarding publication in eLife: if a revision is invited, this decision letter will list the issues that need to be addressed before the manuscript can be accepted.
evidence: This is a description of the content of eLife's decision letters when revisions are requested.

claim: Accepted manuscripts will be formatted, assigned a DOI and posted on the eLife website.
source: Accepted manuscripts will be handled exactly as they are today: they will be formatted, assigned a DOI and posted on the eLife website, with, if appropriate, associated magazine content.
evidence: This is a description of eLife's handling of accepted manuscripts.

claim: Accepted manuscripts may have associated magazine content.
source: Accepted manuscripts will be handled exactly as they are today: they will be formatted, assigned a DOI and posted on the eLife website, with, if appropriate, associated magazine content.
evidence: This is a description of potential additional content for accepted manuscripts.

claim: The decision to accept a manuscript for publication in eLife will become an initial act of curation on a paper that has already been published by the authors.
source: However, the decision to accept a manuscript for publication in eLife will now become an initial act of curation on a paper that has already been published by the authors.
evidence: This is eLife's characterization of how their acceptance decision will function in the new model.

claim: "Selected for inclusion in eLife" will become a sort of badge that eLife attaches to papers.
source: In other words, "selected for inclusion in eLife" will become a sort of badge that we attach to papers.
evidence: This is eLife's description of how their publication decision will be conceptualized.

claim: eLife's long term goal is to render journal title as an indicator of manuscript quality irrelevant as well as obsolete.
source: While pragmatism dictates that we maintain this legacy of print era publishing, our long term goal is to render it irrelevant as well as obsolete.
evidence: This is a direct statement of eLife's long-term objective.

claim: eLife has already begun working on ways to downweight journal title as the main indicator of manuscript quality.
source: We have already begun working on ways to downweight journal title as the main indicator of manuscript quality.
evidence: This is a statement of eLife's current activities.

claim: eLife plans to introduce richer evaluation metrics that can be published alongside articles.
source: We plan, for example, to introduce richer evaluation metrics that can be published alongside articles – both those that we publish in the journal, and those that we review as preprints – ending the absurd process of bouncing from journal to journal until a paper is accepted.
evidence: This is a statement of eLife's planned future development.

claim: The richer evaluation metrics will be published alongside both articles published in the eLife journal and those that eLife reviews as preprints.
source: We plan, for example, to introduce richer evaluation metrics that can be published alongside articles – both those that we publish in the journal, and those that we review as preprints – ending the absurd process of bouncing from journal to journal until a paper is accepted.
evidence: This is a specification of the scope of eLife's planned evaluation metrics.

claim: The process of bouncing from journal to journal until a paper is accepted is absurd.
source: We plan, for example, to introduce richer evaluation metrics that can be published alongside articles – both those that we publish in the journal, and those that we review as preprints – ending the absurd process of bouncing from journal to journal until a paper is accepted.
evidence: This is eLife's characterization of the current publication process.

claim: eLife is developing a new platform for interacting with preprints and public reviews at sciety.org.
source: We are also developing a new platform for interacting with preprints and public reviews (https://sciety.org/).
evidence: This is a statement of eLife's current development activities.

claim: If these changes are widely adopted, they will create a version of the current publishing system that is more efficient, effective and transparent.
source: All of these changes, if widely adopted, will create a version of the current publishing system that is more efficient, effective and transparent.
evidence: This is eLife's prediction about the impact of their changes if adopted widely.

claim: The real opportunities and challenges will come from more radical and dramatic changes to science publishing that will be possible once the field breaks free of the "one paper, one journal, one publication model".
source: But the real opportunities – and challenges – will come from the more radical and dramatic changes to science publishing that will be possible once we finally break free of the "one paper, one journal, one publication model" that still dominates the field.
evidence: This is eLife's perspective on the future potential of publishing reform.

claim: The "one paper, one journal, one publication model" still dominates the field of science publishing.
source: But the real opportunities – and challenges – will come from the more radical and dramatic changes to science publishing that will be possible once we finally break free of the "one paper, one journal, one publication model" that still dominates the field.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of science publishing.

claim: There is no reason for papers to be reviewed only once, or by only one entity.
source: There is no reason for papers to be reviewed only once, or by only one entity.
evidence: This is eLife's argument about the limitations of current review practices.

claim: The review process should involve multiple voices and go on for as long as the work is relevant.
source: The review process should involve multiple voices and go on for as long as the work is relevant.
evidence: This is eLife's vision for how the review process should function.

claim: It should be possible for reviews to be written by anyone with something useful to say about a work, not just the people who have been selected by a journal or other entity.
source: It should be possible for reviews to be written by anyone with something useful to say about a work – not just the people who have been selected by a journal or other entity.

source: And one can imagine all manner of more useful ways to organize and curate the literature than just putting papers into a single "journal".

claim: eLife does not want the evaluation of science to become any more of a popularity contest than it already is.
source: We do not want the evaluation of science to become any more of a popularity contest than it already is, and we want to make sure that the process is as fair and free of bias as humanly possible.

evidence: This is implied by the phrase "any more of a popularity contest than it already is," which presupposes that it is currently a popularity contest to some extent.

claim: eLife wants to make sure that the evaluation process is as fair and free of bias as humanly possible.
source: We do not want the evaluation of science to become any more of a popularity contest than it already is, and we want to make sure that the process is as fair and free of bias as humanly possible.

claim: eLife is committed to observe how the new system is impacting everyone involved in science and medicine.
source: So as we move towards this new system, we also reiterate our commitment to observe how it is impacting everyone involved in science and medicine, and to always be willing to fight for changes that make research communication better for all.
evidence: This is a statement of eLife's commitment to monitoring the impact of their changes.

claim: eLife is committed to always be willing to fight for changes that make research communication better for all.
source: So as we move towards this new system, we also reiterate our commitment to observe how it is impacting everyone involved in science and medicine, and to always be willing to fight for changes that make research communication better for all.
